narrative_reason: The adaptation maps every beat 1:1 — kind girl with dead mother and jealous stepmother, ball announcement, forbidden attendance, fairy godmother transformation, midnight deadline, lost slipper on the staircase, kingdom-wide fitting, triumphant try, forgiveness of stepsisters, and the explicit kindness-and-forgiveness moral — with only culturally incidental substitutions (courtyard chores, couscous/brik, caftans, jasmine garden, sparrows and cats) that do not alter any turning point or the lesson.
safety_reason: A classic Cinderella retelling with only storybook-mild adversity (unkind stepmother, chores, midnight deadline), entirely in English with no unsafe content.
editorial_reason: All characters (kind Cinderella, jealous stepmother, mean stepsisters, fairy godmother, charmed prince) retain their original traits, relationships, and behaviors exactly, and the text is fully in English.
cultural_reason: Names preserved and setting details (jasmine gardens, couscous, caftans, coastal town) feel authentically Tunisian rather than stereotyped, but 'brik' is dropped in as an unexplained food term unlike the broadly familiar 'couscous', leaving one incidental loanword without context.
